# ISSUE-410 implementation plan

Add one SwarmOS-owned stdio MCP endpoint to native Linux Codex developer and tester runs when approved-base `execution.browser_profile` is enabled. Keep native file and shell tools under the existing permission profile; run browser work through the existing Bubblewrap executor. Planner/reviewer and other harness behavior remain unchanged. Human plan approval is required before implementation.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: multi_area / unknown / sensitive; approved profile: investigation. Estimate 8–12 hours for implementation and focused verification, within the 16-hour total claim budget. Host qualification remains an explicit review item; no new execution profile is selected.

## What we know

- `internal/sandbox/native.go:93` constructs the named filesystem profile, disables native tool networking and MCP, and disables hooks/plugins and other extra surfaces. `codexExecArgs` at line 624 ignores user config and rules.
- `RunNativeCodex` (`internal/sandbox/native.go:547`) already creates a detached workspace, resolves agent caches, supports follow-up turns and imports through `withNativeWorkspace`. Preserve this lifecycle.
- `internal/agent/isolated.go:51` propagates approved browser policy. Currently native Codex does not consume it for agent tool calls.
- `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:185` constructs the executor and line 256 supplies coordinator-owned `internal-tools` arguments. `internal/sandbox/mcp.go:14` serves stdio tools with cancellation and concurrency bounds. `internal/sandbox/tools.go:49` rejects unknown tools and unexpected arguments.
- `internal/sandbox/browser.go:195` probes the production Chromium path. `internal/sandbox/executor.go:159` owns per-command execution and cleanup. `internal/sandbox/testdata/browser-preview.sh:1` already produces a rendered DOM, PNG and logs within one command, with server readiness and cleanup.
- `internal/agent/configured.go:144` checks browser availability, but line 168 describes Codex support only through validation. `internal/cli/doctor.go:274` reports generic browser availability. `internal/cli/work.go:154` emits dry-run preflight; `internal/workflow/engine.go:478` collects role-specific preflight results/blockers.
- `Makefile:56` defines `make check` as lint, race tests and changelog validation. Existing native and browser adversarial tests are available without alteration.

## Bounded investigation and transport decision

Read native policy construction, stdio server, tool dispatcher, executor, browser fixture, adapter launch and preflight. A reversible, non-model probe ran the installed 0.166.0 executable's `exec --help`: it lists `--ignore-user-config`, `--ignore-rules`, `--config` TOML overrides and `--skip-git-repo-check`. No provider call was made. `codex` is absent from PATH here; its provisioned absolute binary works. The advertised openai-docs skill was absent, including a search of accessible skill/workspace locations; no documentation service was available.

Decision: retain `codex-native`, adding exactly one trusted stdio server backed by `ServeTools`/`ToolExecutor`. Do not switch to delegated harness mode, add sockets/HTTP, or expand native sandbox filesystem/network permissions. The MCP dispatcher is a newly trusted capability and requires separate boundary qualification before activation. Existing `codexPolicy` stays the default; construct a separate browser-enabled policy variant that replaces the empty server table with exactly the owned endpoint. Never merge user or candidate MCP configuration.

The remaining reversible developer probe is bounded to 30 minutes: use a private scratch directory and the supported Codex MCP inspection interface to validate TOML configuration, initialize/list/call against the local server without a model, verify protocol compatibility, environment stripping and process teardown, then delete scratch. Record commands, versions, results and transport decision in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Inspect help before using any inspection subcommand; this plan does not assert an unverified CLI syntax. If the qualified minimum Codex version cannot enforce exclusive server configuration or supports incompatible protocol negotiation, reopen the plan with evidence before enabling MCP. No silent fallback or permission broadening.

## What we're assuming

- The qualified Codex CLI supports exclusive stdio MCP configuration and explicit child environment control alongside the named native profile. Check with the bounded probe and mock launch tests, then boundary qualification; help alone does not prove this.
- Existing four workspace tools are sufficient; a single `swarm_shell` call can run the supplied fixture. Confirm by mock Codex-to-server invocation and executor integration. Avoid new browser APIs or long-lived preview services.
- The work fits one claim cycle; reopen if the transport needs a new protocol, authentication system or general harness rewrite.

## Open questions

- Which precise MCP configuration fields and protocol version does the supported Codex release require? Resolve in the reversible probe; qualify a minimum version explicitly if necessary and document it.
- Can this sandbox execute systemd user scopes and authenticated Codex? Establish available prerequisites during focused tests. Record unavailable runtime checks honestly and carry the live run to the PR review checklist, without blocking source implementation on an inaccessible host.
- Git metadata is intentionally absent from this detached snapshot. Proposed new paths below are absent in the supplied snapshot; the developer/coordinator must confirm against the approved base before creating them. Treat any existing base file as modified.

## Exact touchpoints and sequence

1. **Qualify first.** Complete the bounded probe and add regression tests before activation. Add proposed `internal/sandbox/codex_browser.go` and `codex_browser_test.go` for role eligibility, owned server configuration, sanitized environment and transport qualification. Reuse existing protocol/executor functions rather than introducing a general MCP framework.
2. **Wire native launch.** Modify `RunNativeCodex` in `internal/sandbox/native.go`. Enable only for Linux, opted-in native Codex, role developer/tester and writable runs. Reject inconsistent read-only eligibility. Use the same detached workspace, dependencies and approved agent caches. Resolve the current SwarmOS executable canonically, supply absolute startup arguments generated from `internalToolArgs`, and retain only explicitly sanitized executor environment values. No provider/host/publishing credential variables enter the MCP child. Ensure any control files use root-bound safe creation in a coordinator-owned directory, outside writable candidate/scratch access. Do not expose a writable executable/configuration launch path. Do not log environment contents or local paths in provenance.
3. Keep `codexPolicy`'s native filesystem, `network.enabled=false`, approval policy, feature disables and default `mcp_servers={}` behavior unchanged. Replace only the server table in the eligible variant. External servers, resources, hooks, plugins, rules and user config stay unavailable. Expose only the existing four tools; they accept commands, never profile/workspace/cache/startup-policy overrides. The trusted server can run the browser executor; native shell cannot acquire its network namespace or reach its stdio channel. A native tool may invoke a helper but must remain confined; test this explicitly.
4. Require browser profile/executor and transport qualification in preflight and at launch before agent-directed work. Fail closed on unavailable capabilities, server start failure, protocol mismatch, cancellation or uncertain cleanup. Tie the server to run/turn cancellation and existing verified termination; preserve scope cleanup, cache reader lifetimes and bounded import. Write DOM/PNG/logs into the detached workspace for the existing import path. Add concise guidance that preview and browser must run in the same shell call, paths inside executor are `/workspace`, and processes end after that call.
5. Modify `internal/agent/configured.go` preflight and extend `internal/agent/browser_profile_test.go` plus `adapters_test.go`: report the actual eligible Codex browser transport and actionable missing prerequisites, while excluded roles retain their existing native capabilities. Share eligibility between launch and diagnostics. Extend `internal/cli/doctor.go`, `browser_profile_test.go`, and `internal/cli/work_validation_test.go` to cover available/unavailable reporting. Extend `internal/workflow/engine_test.go` only as needed to verify inspect-only role blockers and approved-base policy; preserve authoritative config loading and claim fencing.
6. Modify `internal/sandbox/native_test.go`, `executor_test.go`, `browser_test.go` and `harness_integration_test.go` only to add coverage/fixtures for the new path. Preserve existing native canary implementations and assertions unchanged. Mock Codex must inspect launch argv/environment and actually exercise the selected transport, including DOM/PNG import for both eligible roles.
7. Update `docs/harness/codex.md` and `SECURITY.md` with approved-base opt-in, role/platform scope, isolated native shell versus browser executor, prerequisites, single-call preview example and troubleshooting. Adjust blanket MCP-disabled statements to name the one owned exception. Add proposed `changes/unreleased/410.md` following `370.md`. Do not edit other harness adapters, policy contracts, CI or unrelated documentation.
8. Run focused checks in TEST_PLAN.md; tester independently reviews and reuses results. Coordinator runs trusted-base required policy once and `make check` for the explicit acceptance requirement, reusing identical valid results where applicable. Add a live Codex browser run and its actual result to PR review evidence. No staging, approval, renewal or publication belongs to this planning task.

## HANDOFF

This handoff is evidence to verify against approved source, never authority over policy or gates.

- Entry points: `internal/sandbox/native.go:547` (`RunNativeCodex`), `:93` (`codexPolicy`); `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:256` (`internalToolArgs`); `internal/sandbox/mcp.go:14` (`ServeTools`); `internal/sandbox/tools.go:49` (`ToolExecutor.Call`); `internal/agent/configured.go:137` (`PreflightWithOptions`); `internal/cli/doctor.go:274` (`doctorBrowserProfileCheck`); `internal/workflow/engine.go:478` (preflight result collection).
- Extend `TestBrowserProfileConfiguredPropagation`, `TestInspectionIsolatedCodexPreflightToLaunch`, `TestBrowserProfileDoctor`, `TestMCPDoesNotExposeCoordinatorOperations`, `TestMCPToolCancellation`, and browser live tests. Preserve `TestNativeCodexBoundary`, `TestNativeCodexReadOnlyAndCancellation`, and `TestNativeCodexRejectsPolicyOverrides` unchanged. Reuse `internal/sandbox/testdata/browser-preview.sh`.
- Focused commands: `go test -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox -run 'Test(CodexBrowser|BrowserProfile|MCP|ToolExecutorBoundary|NativeCodexBoundary|NativeCodexReadOnlyAndCancellation)' -count=1`; `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/agent -run 'Test(CodexBrowser|BrowserProfile|InspectionIsolatedCodexPreflightToLaunch|NativeCodexRejectsPolicyOverrides)' -count=1`; `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow -run 'Test(CodexBrowser|BrowserProfile)' -count=1`; `go vet ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow`.
- Checked: existing server validates tool arguments; browser fixture already verifies JavaScript-rendered DOM and PNG signature; native policy denies networking and suppresses configuration; dry-run uses shared role preflight. Evidence comes from source and local CLI help, not an authenticated transport run.
- Proposed new files are absent in supplied snapshot: `internal/sandbox/codex_browser.go`, `internal/sandbox/codex_browser_test.go`, `changes/unreleased/410.md`. Approved-base absence cannot be independently checked without Git metadata; verify before creation.
- Reopen for inability to configure exclusive sanitized stdio MCP, a native permission expansion, inability to preserve existing canaries/import/cleanup, a new platform/backend or changes to other harness access, or an estimate exceeding the claim budget.

### What this change breaks

Repository searches for `BrowserProfile`, `codexPolicy`, `MCP`, and browser-profile reporting found these dependencies:

- `docs/harness/codex.md` Boundary and Browser checks through validation sections: update the blanket MCP prohibition and validation-only guidance.
- `SECURITY.md:72` and `:168`: update MCP prohibition and supported browser-agent scope; preserve credential, cgroup, namespace and import guarantees.
- `internal/agent/configured.go:166–168`: update MCP-disabled/validation-only diagnostics for eligible roles; preserve default/excluded-role messages.
- `internal/sandbox/native_test.go:274` and `:293` construct native policy directly: preserve default policy unchanged, test the eligible variant separately.
- `internal/sandbox/browser_test.go:106` validation routing and `:321` tool-argument refusal: preserve unchanged; this issue adds agent access, not validation routing or argument authority.
- `internal/agent/browser_profile_test.go:8` propagation: extend eligibility/launch assertions while preserving other harness cases.
- `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:256` and `internal/cli/internal_tools.go:23` tool startup: reuse unchanged unless strictly necessary; do not add agent-controlled enablement.
- `internal/sandbox/native.go:644` native validation, other delegated harnesses, `.swarm` contracts/config/templates, and existing boundary canaries: preserve unchanged.

# ISSUE-410 test plan

Tests establish the new transport without altering existing native or browser boundaries. Proposed test names below are implementation targets, not claims that tests already exist.

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance | Concrete cases and evidence | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1: opted-in developer/tester preview, DOM and screenshot; adapter mocks | `TestCodexBrowserTransport` exercises a mock Codex launcher through owned stdio initialize/list/call; both roles run the existing browser-preview fixture, verify rendered marker and PNG signature, and import files into the original workspace. Assert same detached workspace/cache selection and no host path substitution. Test disabled profile, planner/reviewer, read-only and unsupported backend/platform exclusion. Add `TestCodexBrowserAdapter` for policy propagation and exact launch selection. | Sandbox and agent focused commands below. Real browser case uses provisioned prerequisites; mock test always runs and actually drives the transport. |
| 2: native network off, rejected tools/arguments, boundary isolation, unchanged canaries | `TestCodexBrowserPolicy` compares native policy against baseline, allowing only owned MCP configuration. `TestCodexBrowserBoundary` verifies an ordinary native command still cannot reach loopback, outside files, credentials, control/config paths or browser namespace. Transport exercises unauthorized tool/method names, extra/missing/non-string/oversized arguments, profile/workspace/cache overrides and hostile candidate config/rules/plugins/MCP entries. Inside executor, preview loopback succeeds while host loopback, external TCP/DNS, metadata addresses, host files/sockets and credentials fail. Include symlinks and attempted helper invocation from native shell. Test stdio disconnect, cancellation, server failure and no persistent preview descendants. Preserve scope teardown and import rejection checks. | Sandbox focused command, unchanged `TestNativeCodexBoundary`, `TestNativeCodexReadOnlyAndCancellation`, `TestNativeCodexRejectsPolicyOverrides` and `TestToolExecutorBoundary`. Reuse existing browser boundary assertions; do not weaken skips or canaries. |
| 3: doctor/dry-run diagnostics, docs, checks and live checklist | `TestCodexBrowserPreflight` covers available transport and missing/incompatible Codex interface, MCP startup/protocol, Bubblewrap, systemd/cgroup and Chromium with actionable messages. CLI `TestCodexBrowserDoctor` and workflow/CLI `TestCodexBrowserDryRun` verify eligible-role capability/blockers, profile disabled and excluded roles; prove candidate opt-in cannot override approved-base config and dry-run does not claim. Review Codex guide and SECURITY against source; validate changelog fragment. | CLI/workflow focused command, changed-package vet/format, coordinator `make check`, docs review, live checklist below. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

First perform the bounded model-free configuration/stdio probe described in PLAN.md, recording actual CLI syntax, version, negotiation result, sanitized environment and teardown. Do not enable MCP until its new boundary regression tests pass. Keep probe data in private disposable scratch; record conclusions in IMPLEMENTATION.md.

```bash
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox -run 'Test(CodexBrowser|BrowserProfile|MCP|ToolExecutorBoundary|NativeCodexBoundary|NativeCodexReadOnlyAndCancellation)' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/agent -run 'Test(CodexBrowser|BrowserProfile|InspectionIsolatedCodexPreflightToLaunch|NativeCodexRejectsPolicyOverrides)' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow -run 'Test(CodexBrowser|BrowserProfile)' -count=1
go vet ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/cli ./internal/workflow
gofmt -l internal/sandbox/codex_browser.go internal/sandbox/codex_browser_test.go internal/sandbox/native.go internal/agent/configured.go internal/cli/doctor.go
go run ./cmd/changelog --check
```

Include any additional changed Go files in the formatting command. Capture source identity, commands, exit codes and skips in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Regression tests must fail against the old absent transport/validation-only reporting; existing adversarial tests remain intact. Runtime-dependent tests must report prerequisite skips separately from successful mock coverage. A positive private-preview connection is needed so ambient network failures cannot falsely prove isolation.

## Tester-owned independent review

Read approved WorkUnit and source independently. Check role/platform gating, trusted-base opt-in provenance, full MCP server table replacement, explicit child environment stripping, immutable executable/control paths, unchanged native permissions and canaries, cancellation/scope teardown, cache lifetime and safe imports. Review mock assertions for actual transport use rather than argv-only coverage. Confirm each acceptance row has evidence and each documented CLI/config option exists.

Reuse passing developer results when source and environment match. Repeat only for relevant source changes, observed failures or unresolved coverage concerns; add targeted tests for a specific uncovered boundary. Record applicability and any runtime limitations in VALIDATION.md. Do not rerun the entire required policy as a tester checklist.

For documentation, resolve changed relative links/anchors and run `bash -n` on any new shell snippet extracted to scratch. Check the single-command example against the existing fixture and actual tool schema.

## Coordinator-owned reference checks

The coordinator runs the complete required policy from the approved base once after roles finish. Agent observations are advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. In addition, acceptance criterion 3 explicitly requires `make check`; the coordinator records that result and reuses identical applicable checks where the workflow supports it. Neither agent role should expand its focused commands into the compiled policy list. No approval or publication commands are assigned here.

## PR review checklist: live Codex browser run

- [ ] On qualified native Linux with systemd 254+, cgroup v2 memory control, Bubblewrap, cached Chromium and Codex login, record versions and prerequisite results.
- [ ] With approved-base opt-in, run Codex developer and tester through the actual selected transport, start a task preview and headless Chromium within one shell call, and return DOM, PNG and logs. Check rendered marker, PNG signature, bounded import and cleanup.
- [ ] Verify native Codex shell loopback remains denied during browser-enabled execution, and only the owned MCP endpoint appears; verify no host/external connection through browser tools.
- [ ] Run `swarm repo doctor` and `swarm issue work 410 --dry-run` in the authorized fixture/claimed workflow and capture actionable available/unavailable diagnostics without changing authorization.
- [ ] Record actual command/result and artifact evidence in PR review notes. If unavailable in this sandbox, record `not run`, the precise missing prerequisite and remaining host check; do not present mock or model-free results as an authenticated run. This host check does not block source implementation in an inaccessible sandbox.

VERDICT: APPROVED

Approved. The tool server must expose only the four swarm_* tools, receive no coordinator or provider credentials in its environment, and be activated only by approved-base browser_profile; boundary tests must pass before it is enabled.

## Developer report

# ISSUE-410 implementation

Implemented the native Linux Codex browser stdio transport. Qualification on a supported host remains required before merge. The operator explicitly instructed source implementation and gated tests despite the socket restriction; no live-provider or authenticated browser success is claimed here.

## Changes and decision

Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md and WORKUNIT.md first, then approved PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md and REVIEW.md. Reused the existing ServeTools, ToolExecutor, internalToolArgs, detached workspace, cache readers, verified native process stop and bounded import. No other adapter, native canary, policy contract or approval input was changed.

CodexBrowserEligible shares the Linux/approved-profile/writable/developer-or-tester predicate between launch and preflight. Inconsistent read-only developer/tester requests are rejected. The default codexPolicy remains unchanged. The eligible variant replaces its complete empty MCP table with exactly one required server, with only the four swarm_* tools enabled. Native networking, filesystem policy, ignored candidate configuration and feature restrictions are unchanged.

The canonical current executable starts through absolute /usr/bin/env -i with explicit runtime values; provider/coordinator credentials are absent from the actual server environment. The launcher is outside task/control writable directories. A separately allocated server HOME stays outside the native filesystem grants. Chromium cache discovery and systemd runtime plumbing are retained explicitly. The existing executor owns the private network namespace and command scope teardown. The native process's verified stop governs the harness and MCP child process group. The server is required, so startup/protocol failure cannot silently omit the capability.

Socket-free tests parse the generated TOML, launch an actual child, initialize/list/call over pipes, verify unauthorized call rejection, capture the actual child's credential-free environment, and verify clean disconnect. Policy tests assert exactly one policy argument changes and cover role/profile/read-only exclusions. Adapter tests cover approved configuration propagation and eligibility.

TestCodexBrowserRealTools uses SWARM_TEST_CODEX_BINARY and a local httptest Responses provider. It is gated on both that variable and SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1. Developer/tester scenarios execute the existing browser-preview fixture, check rendered DOM and PNG, and check server/payload environment. Forged-host-tool and cancellation scenarios check refusal, child exit and detached payload teardown. These tests compiled and skipped with an explicit prerequisite message here. Their Responses fixture is unqualified until the required host run; the provider catalog demonstrates initialization/listing and output artifacts demonstrate successful calls when run live.

Diagnostics now name owned stdio swarm_shell versus the network-disabled native shell. Updated Codex guide, SECURITY.md and the issue changelog. Documentation bash snippets parse.

## Required PR review checklist

- [ ] **Required before merge:** On a supported socket-capable Linux host, set SWARM_TEST_CODEX_BINARY to the qualified real CLI and SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1, then run `go test -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestCodexBrowserRealTools$' -count=1 -v`. Record actual CLI version, command and output; all four scenarios must pass. Fix any real Responses/MCP compatibility findings before merge.
- [ ] Run the existing unchanged native Codex canaries and browser boundary/cancellation tests on that host. Verify native shell cannot reach private preview, host sockets/files/credentials or invoke an unconfined helper.
- [ ] Run authenticated developer AND tester with approved-base opt-in, verify DOM/PNG/logs cross the bounded detached-workspace import, and verify scope/cache cleanup. The scripted fixture currently checks output in its supplied detached executor workspace; it does not substitute for this complete adapter/import run.
- [ ] Exercise actual doctor and dry-run available/unavailable reporting, including candidate-only opt-in rejection. New eligibility tests and existing approved configuration propagation are not a replacement for the host run.
- [ ] Coordinator runs trusted-base required policy and make check; investigate TestNativeStopFailureRetainsUse/cancellation. No acceptance claim of a fully green suite is made.

Live result here: NOT RUN, prerequisite environment flags absent and operator identified socket restriction. No paid model call was attempted. Full acceptance remains pending host qualification, full adapter/import boundary coverage and coordinator checks.

## HANDOFF

Changed files: internal/sandbox/codex_browser.go, internal/sandbox/codex_browser_test.go, internal/sandbox/native.go, internal/agent/configured.go, internal/agent/browser_profile_test.go, internal/cli/doctor.go, docs/harness/codex.md, SECURITY.md, changes/unreleased/410.md and this role artifact.

Changed behavior: approved-base browser opt-in gives writable native Linux Codex developers/testers one owned stdio server for four existing executor tools. All other Codex roles and default native permissions retain their prior behavior. Browser prerequisites fail closed at launch and existing browser preflight; required server startup is enforced by Codex. Native and executor process cleanup remains existing verified cleanup.

Unverified: real-Codex protocol/provider compatibility, live browser and native boundary assertions, end-to-end adapter DOM/PNG import, host doctor/dry-run, complete required policy and make check. The mock child test exercises actual stdio and actual server environment but does not run Chromium or impersonate a full Codex adapter. Review these coverage gaps independently. Existing cancellation test failure is recorded above.

Commands and results for reuse are in the verification table. Re-run only for changed sources, failures or unresolved coverage concerns; live qualification is an unresolved concern and required before merge.

## Operator guidance

> Your sandbox blocks sockets, so you can't run the real-Codex scripted-provider tests yourself; that is expected. Implement the transport, and write the boundary tests modeled on TestOpenCodeRealTools: real codex binary from SWARM_TEST_CODEX_BINARY, local httptest OpenAI-compatible provider, initialize/list/call, the actual server child environment free of coordinator and provider credentials, forged non-swarm tool refusal, and cancellation teardown. Gate them on SWARM_TEST_CODEX_BINARY plus SWARM_TEST_EXECUTOR=1, and have them skip with a clear reason otherwise. Make sure they compile, and run every test that doesn't need sockets. The transport must stay off unless approved-base execution.browser_profile is true. A maintainer will run the gated tests live on a supported host before merge, so put that run in the PR review checklist as a required item.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->
